name: hardcore
title: Hardcore
description: Fast four-on-the-floor music with a heavily distorted kick, dark or anthemic leads and screeches. Covers mainstream hardcore; uptempo and frenchcore push the same ideas further.

structure.description: Kick and percussion for mixing in; tease the main motif late in the intro.
Kick out; atmosphere, pads or a vocal set the mood.
Kick roll or snare roll speeding up into the drop.
Kick on every beat with the main lead or screech riff; short phrases repeated with variations.
Melodic section with the main melody over chords, kick out or half-time.
Shorter and more intense than the first.
Main riff again, with a variation or a new layer.
Kick and percussion for mixing out.

rhythms.name: four on the floor
rhythms.description: Kick on every beat through drops, intros and outros.

rhythms.name: kick gallop fill
rhythms.description: Extra 16th kicks at the end of the bar to mark a phrase ending.

rhythms.name: offbeat bass
rhythms.description: Bass on the off-beat 8ths between kicks, the frenchcore signature.

rhythms.name: kick roll
rhythms.description: Two-bar roll into a drop; music_roll gives smooth acceleration.

rhythms.name: stab riff
rhythms.description: Short syncopated lead or screech stabs against the kick.

progressions.description: Dramatic ending on a major V, borrowed from harmonic minor (its raised 7th is the leading tone back to i).
Eastern-sounding darkness with a major tonic.

guidance: The kick is harder and more distorted than in hardstyle, with a punchy, often less tonal tail; still tune it to the key's root.
At these tempos melodies breathe: fewer, longer notes and repeated short riffs read better than busy lines.
Drops lean on rhythm: short lead or screech stabs in syncopation with the kick, repeated and varied every 4 or 8 bars.
Build tension with kick rolls that speed up (music_roll) and end with a short gap before the drop.

Uptempo (roughly 190-220 BPM) uses extremely distorted kicks, often with the kick itself carrying a melody. Frenchcore (roughly 190-200 BPM) adds the offbeat bass and often live-sounding drums, pianos or strings.
Work in 8, 16 and 32-bar phrases and change something at each boundary.
